pull_request.title: Software: plot native tracker coverage and material for issue 38
pull_request.head: codex/issue38-validation-review
pull_request.body:
Answers Markus Elsing's October 14 request in #38 with actual native DD4hep/ROOT tracker plots: sensor crossings and logical stations/holes versus eta/phi, including direct z=0 maps, and stacked X/X0 and L/lambda_I versus eta. Includes the full represented passive/support/cooling/service material, reproducible tooling and compressed per-ray evidence.

The scan uses 7,872 main B=0 rays plus 576 separate offset-phi controls at three stated z vertices. It distinguishes shared pixel substrates, long-strip sensor pairs and ideal station-ID holes. Current-datum ideal references are explicitly separate from historical study denominators. The offset control exposes missed holes; the maximum 4.87848 X0 service-dominated material result is retained. These are finite geometric diagnostics, not reconstructed hit efficiency or engineering acceptance.

Start with [results and plots](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/issue38-validation-review/docs/validation/issue38-review/results.md). [PR #82](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/82) separately explains strip mounting and the mechanical/service interfaces.

Validation: all 45,646 native sensitive patches match expected transforms/bounds; analytic pipe path, category closure and independent material-path reintegration pass; repeated full ray arrays are identical; six unit controls pass and are added to CI. Separate PhysVal assessment verifies all 8,448 ray identities and independent box intersections for 262 selected rays with no discrepancies. Project/session records and token-site validation/build pass. Detector geometry and material definitions are unchanged.

Refs #38.

comments.body:
Comment from @MarkusElsing - Figure 2.7 shows way too much silicon overlap:

Figure 2.7 seems to show a really large overlap in silicon. Please try to optimize the module arrangement for discs such that the silicon overlap is around at max X %), still ensuring full coverage. You can modify the sensor design - under restriction of still using an RD53 based sensor, the number of modules in phi and the number of rings, however, the overall disk coverage should be unchanged.
Estimate the change of cable and cooling envelopes for the updated setup.

Disk positions (Table 1.4) are optimized to the 3rd digit, this is far too over-optimized.

Suggested new positions:
615, 795, 1046, 1333, 1645, 1977, 2328, 2692, 3070 

In the future, if optimizations are due, please floor them to the `mm` precision.

New review comments form Reviewer Susanne Kuehn:


* Questionable and not clear are a few phrases: what are graphite shims (line 27)? line 35 introduces a slim barrel which only becomes clear what it is on the next page, what are guards in line 105?, Table 2.2 lists a datum which should be radius. Table 2.4 lists also datums which are this time z-values.

* It doesn't say how staves are mounted. One could ask for a figure. The structural body for the staves could be drawn (p.9) and then also the stiffness be calculated or details added what its stiffness has to be and by this thickness of mechanical parts.

* A cooling estimate is given at the end. Why are stave run at -35C and the endcaps at -40C. 
lien 227 speaks of a raised graphite feed: a picture would be good. similar for the tongues mentioned in figure 9.

* The glue to attach carbon and silicon modules is included in Fig 2.8 for endcaps but seems to be missing for the staves (Fig 2.3.). 

* Request for clarification of Services: a picture, how the connection of pigtails is foreseen would be good (lines 313-319).

New review comments/questions from Markus Elsing: - Request for coverage plots: nhits vs eta and phi, hole plots vs eta and phi - Request for : x0 und L0 vs eta (stacked, see uploaded example) - Request for explanaition how the strips are mounted

Response to Susanne Kuehn's forwarded October 14 review: the point-by-point answers and concrete documentation changes are in **PR #82**. It includes an 18-page compiled review extract, editable replacement text against the current TDR revision, and four new schematic pages. The attachment here is an older pixel edition, so the corrections target the current selected layout rather than restoring its obsolete ring/count tables.

- **Terminology and table headings:** graphite shims are the thermal spacers from the ASIC backs to the support-side module plane. “Slim” now means the longitudinal inactive sensor edge; “guard” means silicon excluded from the geometric active map, without claiming a fabricated guard-ring design. Barrel/disc headings explicitly identify radius and reference z position.
- **Stave mounting and stiffness:** the drawing follows module → cooled sandwich/spine → CFRP foot → bearing ring → cage/end support, and identifies the axial locator versus proposed sliding contacts. The rings are coupled parts of a cage, not six independently grounded beam bearings. The response gives the recorded displacement screens, the required-EI equation and historical span-sensitivity examples. Cage section/laminate, joint stiffness and load cases are still missing engineering inputs, so a qualified cage thickness or current-baseline sag is not claimed.
- **Cooling and graphite feet/tongues:** −35°C barrel and −40°C endcap are separate thermal-screen assumptions. The warmer endcap sensitivity fails in retained cases; a common operating temperature needs contact/leakage/hydraulic closure. The new drawing separates the solid raised graphite **foot** (no coolant) from the three structural disc **tongues**.
- **Glue:** the stave material already includes a 0.100 mm epoxy interface and 0.080 mm-equivalent internal adhesive; the module's flex epoxy is separate. The missing drawing/wording now shows these allocations. Actual ASIC-to-shim and mounting-joint bonds still need specification; no glue mass was silently added.
- **Pigtails:** the new diagram traces the proposed module termination to the barrel bundle/collector, and the endcap's own-face tail → bus → radial fan → rim collector/trunk. Connector heads, pinouts, strain relief, slots and bend/access qualification remain open.

PR #82 also clarifies standalone pixel versus combined tracker passive-aperture dimensions. Its source/drawing consistency review corrections are applied; pdfLaTeX compilation and rendered-page inspection pass. These changes answer the presentation questions and expose the remaining engineering work; they do not constitute mechanical, thermal or electrical qualification.

[Response, source locators and compiled-review links](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/issue38-mechanics-review/docs/publication/issue38-mechanics/README.md).

Response to Markus Elsing's forwarded October 14 review: **PR #83** supplies the requested plots and their reproducible native scan; **PR #82** separately explains how the short- and long-strip barrels and petals mount to their supports.

1. **nhits and holes versus eta/phi:** the plots include direct eta×phi maps, separate z=0 maps and eta/phi projections. Active chip patches, physical sensors and logical stations are distinguished. Pixel islands sharing a substrate are deduplicated; a long-strip station requires both faces of the same module. Holes are missing ideal **station IDs**, so extra overlap hits cannot cancel a hole in another station.
2. **Stacked X0 and L0 versus eta:** both radiation-length X/X0 and interaction-length L/lambda_I plots integrate the actual native DD4hep/ROOT volumes, including the represented supports, electronics, cooling and services. The stack separates subsystem ownership and shared services; it is not restricted to the silicon slabs of an ACTS surface approximation.
3. **Strip mounting:** PR #82 includes a comparison table and load-path diagrams for all four assemblies: single-face short-strip pickups and stave/petal contacts; paired long-strip faces on one structural sandwich, keyed/potted barrel contacts and the three petal seats. Sliding constraints and unqualified cage/joint reactions are explicit.

The scan actually ran **7,872 main rays plus 576 separate offset-phi controls**: B=0, x=y=0, z=−150/0/+150 mm, eta −4…4 in 0.2 steps and 64 phi samples. These are finite geometric crossings, not reconstructed-hit efficiency. The ideal reference uses declared active bounds and current disc datums, explicitly distinguished from earlier frozen-study denominators.

The adverse results are retained: maximum two sampled holes, grid-phase sensitivity including central gaps missed by the first grid, and material up to **4.87848 X0**, dominated by represented services. These motivate further service/coverage review; the model was not tuned to reduce the plotted values. Native inventory, analytic pipe-path and material-accounting controls pass. A separate scientific consistency assessment checked every ray's ideal/count/material identities and independently checked sensor intersections for 262 selected rays with zero discrepancies.

[Plots, exact sample, results and provenance](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/issue38-validation-review/docs/validation/issue38-review/results.md) · [Mounting explanations and compiled review](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/issue38-mechanics-review/docs/publication/issue38-mechanics/README.md).

The earlier integer disc positions and overlap/layout follow-ups are already merged through PR #40 and PR #46. Issue #38 remains open for reviewer assessment and the explicit outstanding engineering questions.

coverage.prompts: Available account-matched user-visible messages, public Codex inputs and curated journal excerpts. Historical full input coverage is unknown.

coverage.token_accounting: References only. Never sum accounts across PRs or assign a shared turn by text length.
coverage.unknowns: Unrecorded names, models, tools, subagent identities and response links remain unknown; empty lists are not zero activity.
coverage.remote: Snapshot, not live synchronization; deleted/edited history and emoji reactions are not recovered.
coverage.branch_only: Pinned branch journal snapshots are references, not imported counters. Unretained or other-device inputs remain unknown.
